Variables are plain configuration, visible in logs. Secrets are encrypted and masked. Publishable values (e.g. VITE_ keys that ship in the bundle anyway) → variables. Anything that grants privileges → secrets.

column1: Why are VITE_-prefixed env vars never secret?
column2: Vite inlines them into the client JavaScript bundle at build time; every visitor can read them.

column1: Supabase publishable key vs secret (service-role) key
column2: Publishable: safe in the browser; access is limited by Row Level Security. Secret/service-role: bypasses RLS; must only live on servers.

column1: Blameless postmortem: what goes in it?

column1: Why is "human error" never a root cause?
column2: It stops the analysis where it should start: ask why the system let a human make that error unnoticed, and fix the system.

column1: How does a deep-equality check terminate on cycles?
column2: Keep a map of (a, b) pairs already under comparison; meeting a pair again means "assume equal so far" instead of recursing forever.

column1: Why must a test runner run tests in one file sequentially by default?
column2: Tests share module-level state (e.g. a singleton store). Interleaving async tests would let one test's state leak into another's, causing order-dependent failures.

column1: A Tale of Two Clocks: the two clocks
column2: The JS timer (setTimeout/setInterval): imprecise, can be delayed or throttled. The audio clock (AudioContext.currentTime): sample-accurate. Schedule on the audio clock; use JS timers only to wake up and schedule ahead.

column1: Metronome: why LOOKAHEAD (150 ms) ≫ SCHEDULER_INTERVAL (25 ms)?
column2: So that if a wake-up is late (main thread busy), the next clicks are already scheduled on the audio clock. If they were equal, any delay in a wake-up would make a click late.

column1: What does Web Audio do with start(t) when t is already in the past?
column2: It starts immediately, so the sound is late by (currentTime − t).
